mappings.note: Asks what the WRITER holds to be the defining trait of nawabs as a class (thinking oneself above others) -- the piece read as a comment on a class. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no single narrated event states this generalisation; it is Yashpal's judgement.
How the Nawab got the taste (by smelling) -- plain incident recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the writer's irony about the act is not what is graded.
The bhaav (asantosh) in the Nawab's eyes on the narrator's entry -- direct detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no mantavya is probed.
What the Nawab offered the narrator to eat -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content only.

What the Nawab could not stomach (being seen travelling second class) -- character feeling as stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the student reports the feeling instead of appraising the satire on it.
Which class of ticket the narrator took -- plain fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft element.
What the Nawab did with the kheera after preparing it. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as the item stops at the action.
Whom the narrator was watching out of the corner of his eye. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: bare detail, no authorial intent.
Whose habit it was to sit idle and imagine (the narrator's) -- character attribution. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because nothing about shaili is asked.
What the Nawab had bought to pass the solitary journey. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: plain content.
The reason the narrator gave for declining the kheera -- recall of his stated words. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because his real self-respecting motive, not the writer's purpose, is at issue.
Why the Nawab threw the kheeras out of the window -- character motive. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the item asks for the character's reason and not for the writer's comment on nawabi display.
Which sudden act (the change of manner) displeased the narrator -- narrative detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the reason it displeased him is a separate long-answer item.
Who at Lucknow station knows the way to use a kheera (the sellers) -- text fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no appraisal required.
Who began the conversation -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as nothing about bhasha-shaili is tested.

Authorship identification of the path (Yashpal) -- literary/bibliographic knowledge. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because this frame carries no biography or authorship LO, so the competency is the honest citation rather than an LO the item does not meet.
Why the narrator bought a second-class ticket (to think about his new story in solitude) -- stated reason. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the nayi-kahani satire is carried by a different item.
The narrator's reply to the offer of kheera -- direct recall of dialogue. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no style judgement is involved.
Stem itself declares 'latherh lena' a muhavara and asks its meaning -- idiomatic usage. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the episode containing the idiom is not needed to answer.
How the Nawab made the kheera fit to eat (peeled, sliced, sprinkled salt/jeera/mirch) -- sequence of described actions. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: procedure recall, no craft.
The preparations before eating (towel spread, washing, wiping) -- narrated detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the nafasat this displays is appraised in other items, not this one.
Meaning of 'ehtiyaat' as used in the lesson -- shabdarth in context. Rejected C-H1.2 because the item is not framed as a paryayvachi drill; the companion item that IS so framed carries C-H1.2.

Why the writer says the Lucknow sellers know how to use a kheera -- the answer is the factual detail that they supply jeera-salt and ground mirch. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the reason sought is circumstantial, not a statement of mantavya.
Where the Nawab's lota was kept -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no interpretive demand.

Two-mark item on how the Nawab looked at the glistening slices (trishna-bhari aankhon se) -- text detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the phrase is recalled, not appraised as shaili. (Stem is malformed: it carries its options inline and is typed very_short -- defect reported, mapped on meaning.)
Where the Nawab was from (Lucknow) -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft element.
What the Nawab had bought to eat. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as plain content recall.
Who cut the kheera -- agent of a narrated action. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no authorial intent.
Meaning of 'udar' (pet) as used in the lesson -- shabdarth in context. Rejected C-H1.2 because no grammar category (paryayvachi/vilom/muhavara) is being drilled.

Framed explicitly as a paryayvachi item for 'ehtiyaat', which this book files under grammatical and lexical usage. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the drill is a synonym task, not comprehension of the path.

The Nawab's attitude on seeing the narrator -- character reaction. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: plain content. (Printed key 'dukhi' sits oddly against the text's 'asantosh'; mapped on the question, not the key.)
Meaning of 'sakeel' inside the Nawab's quoted line -- word sense in context. Rejected C-H1.2 as it is not a paryayvachi/vilom/muhavara task.
Meaning of 'tahzeeb' from the lesson's vocabulary. Rejected C-H1.2 because the item asks the shabdarth of a path word, not a grammar structure.
Meaning of 'nafasat' from the lesson's vocabulary. Rejected C-H1.2 for the same reason as its sibling shabdarth items.
Meaning of 'nazakat' from the lesson's vocabulary. Rejected C-H1.2: shabdarth in context, not grammatical usage.
Meaning of 'nafees' from the lesson's vocabulary. Rejected C-H1.2 on the same ground as the other shabdarth items in this set.
Meaning of 'mufassil' as used in the lesson. Rejected C-H1.2 because the item tests a path word's sense, not a grammar category.
Why, per the narrator, the Nawab bought a second-class ticket -- inference supported by the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because it asks a character's reason, not the writer's comment on the class.

Causes of the Nawab's embarrassment about the kheera, all from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as the options report character reasons rather than Yashpal's critique. (Near-duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter -- reported.)
What the Nawab did after throwing the kheera away (lay down tired) -- narrated action. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: plain content.

Asks the student to judge how far the Nawab's sanak can be justified and why -- a critical response to the attitude the piece holds up for satire. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no answer can be built from narrated facts alone; it needs an appraisal of what Yashpal is exposing.

Path-anchored abhivyakti question: starting from the sanak the lesson describes, the student reasons about positive obsessions. LO-1 explicitly covers abhivyakti-based questions on the prescribed gadya. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the answer is the student's own reasoning, not an appreciation of Yashpal's satire or style.
Why the Nawab looked at the narrator with proud, pink eyes -- motive of a narrated gesture. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the item asks about the character's moment, not the writer's purpose.
Asks the student to explain the vyangya on nawabi parampara carried through the character -- squarely the writer's intent. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because retelling the incidents does not answer it.

A shabd-chitra of the kheera preparation AS GIVEN IN THE TEXT -- content plus expression, which LO-1 names. Rejected C-H1.4 because the material is entirely the path's, not the student's own composition subject.
Which gestures show the Nawab was not keen to talk -- evidence gathering from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as the gestures are reported, not appraised as craft.

The lesson only supplies the model; the answer is the student's own descriptive composition about preparing a favourite food. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no part of the required answer comes from the path's vishayvastu -- it is srijanatmak lekhan.

Which of the Nawab's hav-bhav made the narrator feel he was not keen to talk -- text evidence. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content recall. (Duplicate in substance of another 3-mark item in this chapter -- reported.)

Charitra-chitran: what kind of person the Nawab appears to be. Characters fall under LO-1 by this book's policy. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the sketch is built from the character's acts, not from an appraisal of Yashpal's mantavya.

Asks for the proofs of khandani tahzeeb, nafasat and nazakat that the narrator saw, 'path ke aadhar par' -- evidence from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the item wants the evidence, not a judgement on the writer's irony.

Requires characterising the samanti jeevan-shaili the piece exhibits and arguing whether it can survive today -- engaging the text as a comment on a class. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because a recital of the Nawab's actions does not answer the 'tarksahit' part.
Why the narrator avoided the Nawab's eyes (seeing his disinterest) -- stated reason. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: plain comprehension.

General abhivadan etiquette -- when a greeting should be made -- with no anchor in this path and no written or creative product. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because nothing in the prose text answers it; rejected C-H1.2 because courtesy convention is not a vyakaranik structure and C-H1.4 because nothing is to be written. It falls to the goal-level oral/courtesy skill.

Names the target of the writer's kataksh (the decaying samanti class) -- authorial intent, the piece as a comment on a class. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the target is never stated as a narrative fact.

Yashpal's year and place of birth -- author biography. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the frame has no biography LO and the item tests nothing of the path's vishayvastu, so the competency is the honest citation.
Where Yashpal took his B.A. -- author biography. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 for the same reason: no biography LO exists in this frame, and no part of the prose text answers it.
Which title is NOT a work of Yashpal -- bibliography / literary history. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the frame has no bibliography LO, so the competency is the honest citation.
Which class the narrator travelled in on the passenger train -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft element.
Why asantosh rose in the Nawab's eyes -- stated cause. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the event, not the writer's purpose, is being tested.

What the narrator supposed on seeing the Nawab's manner -- narrative recall of a thought. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the keyed thought is a plot guess, unlike the companion item whose keyed thought is Yashpal's evaluative reflection.
